overview: Black plays 1...Nc6, and after 2.d5 retreats with 2...Nb8, losing two tempi and handing White a free space gain. It is more a curiosity than a real defence; after 2...Nb8 White just continues development with a comfortable edge.

white_ideas.idea: Take advantage of the extra tempi with quick development
Keep the d5 space gain and play c4 and Nc3
Build a normal centre with e4

black_ideas.idea: Challenge the d5 pawn with ...c6 or ...e6

typical_structures.structure: White pawn on d5 gaining space against a normal Black set-up

character.notes: Slow; White is just ahead in space and time.

gambit.notes: No material is given on purpose in the main line.

soundness.notes: Not a serious defence; Black simply loses time.

structure.notes: Centre undecided and pawn structure standard.

approach.notes: Almost never chosen by strong players.

level.notes: Little to learn but a waste of tempi, not a repertoire choice.

character.reason: A calm position where White simply leads in time.

soundness.reason: Black wastes two moves on the knight excursion.

plans.reason: White has the extra space from d5.
